note: The assistant add-on: a chat with the agents connected to the app, to include. A launcher at the bottom right opens a panel where the person asks in plain words (the ask step), the agents answer (ask:reply), and the proposals they open come back as cards to preview, accept or reject, as does every other proposal waiting for review: this is where the person reviews. Everything here is named assistant..., so it merges into any screen; an app restyles it by overriding the assistant.* tokens. See README.md.

assistantFile.note: A file as a card, as chat apps show attachments: an icon of its kind (a picture, a sound, any other file), its name, and its length (a sound) or size; removable from the files of the next message

runs.text: {{file.duration != null ? floor(file.duration / 60) + ':' + pad(floor(file.duration % 60), 2) : (file.size ?? 0) >= 1048576 ? formatNumber(file.size / 1048576, 0, 1) + ' MB' : (file.size ?? 0) >= 1024 ? formatNumber(floor(file.size / 1024)) + ' KB' : (file.size ?? 0) + ' B'}}

assistantPointedChip.note: An element the person pointed at, as a chip: its type and where it is written (a program's definition, or a document's node), never what it shows; the tooltip says when it stands for more than itself. Removable from the next message's, and with a button that shows its source where the host has the window for it

assistantPast.note: A past conversation in the list: its title and when it was, a click goes on with it, and a button deletes it (beside it, so its click is its own)

assistantExtras.note: What a proposal adds beside its edits: its assets (a file card each, with a picture's thumbnail while it is previewed) and its run-once steps, a line each

children.text: {{step.note ?? (step.image == 'open' || step.image == 'openAsset' ? t('assistant.opens', {name: step.with.asset ?? step.asset ?? ''}) : t('assistant.runs', {step: slice((keys(step)[0] ?? '') + ' ' + text(values(step)[0] ?? ''), 0, 80)}))}}

assistant.start.note: What the host was asked to ask (its --ask) starts a conversation of its own: the one before is kept with the past ones

then.value: {{ {kind: 'files', mine: true, files: state.assistant.attachments, time: now()} }}
{{ {kind: 'pointed', mine: true, items: state.assistant.pointed, time: now()} }}

assistant.ask.value: {{ {mine: true, from: t('assistant.you'), text: text, time: now(), error: false} }}

assistant.ask.options: {{state.assistant.models != null && state.assistant.models.default != '' ? {model: some(state.assistant.models.models, it.id == state.assistant.model) ? state.assistant.model : state.assistant.models.default} : {}}}

assistant.attach.note: The file dialog: what the person picks lands in picked, and the watch adds it to the next message's files

assistant.drop.note: with: files, dropped on the panel from the OS (onDrop's event.files): attached like picked ones

assistant.attachFailed.note: with: message, why a file couldn't be attached (its type, its size): said in the conversation

assistant.attachFailed.value: {{ {mine: false, from: t('assistant.title'), text: message, time: now(), error: true} }}

assistant.point.note: Lets the person point at an element of the app for the next message, four at most: the panel steps aside (it is modal), the focus staying where it was, and comes back when they pick or cancel

assistant.pointed.note: When the person picked: the element joins the next message's (once: one already there, or the assistant's own, is forgotten again), and the panel opens on the field

assistant.pointCancelled.note: When the person cancels pointing: the panel as it was

assistant.unpoint.note: with: id. Takes an element from the next message's: the engine forgets its record

assistant.keepCurrentPoints.note: Drops the elements pointed at before the latest commit, quietly: where they were may have moved

assistant.showSource.note: with: record, an element pointed at. Asks the host to show where it is written (its changes window's Source page); a host without it does nothing

ask:reply.value: {{ {mine: false, from: event.from, text: length(event.error ?? '') > 0 ? event.error : event.text ?? '', time: event.time, error: length(event.error ?? '') > 0, asked: find(requests, it.id == event.request).text ?? ''} }}

do.value: {{ {kind: 'card', id: proposal.id, time: event.time, title: proposal.message, summary: t('assistant.touches', {n: length(proposal.touches ?? [])}), lines: slice(proposal.changes ?? [], 0, 3)} }}

then.value: {{ {kind: 'extras', id: proposal.id, time: event.time, assets: slice(proposal.assets ?? [], 0, 8), run: slice(proposal.run ?? [], 0, 8)} }}

assistant.stop.note: Stops the requests in progress (cancelAsk): the agents are told, and what they send after is dropped

assistant.stop.value: {{ {mine: false, from: t('assistant.title'), text: t('assistant.stopped'), time: now(), error: false, note: true, asked: find(requests, it.id == state.assistant.pending).text ?? ''} }}

assistant.retry.note: with: text, the request a reply answered (or a stopped one): asked again, as it was written

assistant.copy.note: with: text and at, a message and its place: copied, and its button says so for a moment

assistant.review.note: with: id. Asks the host for its own window on the change (ChangesWindow): the file by file diff

assistant.loadModels.note: The host's read-only assistant.models: the provider in use, the person's default and the models to choose from. Only the hosts whose own agent is connected (the peer 'agent') have it; without it (MCP-only setups, other hosts, the rendering check) models stays null and the picker hides

assistant.pickModel.note: The person's default is kept as '': it follows a later change of the default in the Launcher's Settings

assistant.clear.note: Forgets the conversation, without keeping it with the past ones

assistant.keep.note: Keeps the conversation with the past ones, newest first and 50 at most, in place of its earlier copy: titled by its first request, on one line, and dated by its last message

then.to: {{slice(concat([{id: state.assistant.conversation != '' ? state.assistant.conversation : text(now()), title: slice(join(split(find(state.assistant.messages, it.mine == true && length(it.text ?? '') > 0).text ?? find(state.assistant.messages, length(it.text ?? '') > 0).text ?? t('assistant.messages'), '\n'), ' '), 0, 80), time: slice(state.assistant.messages, -1)[0].time ?? now(), count: count(state.assistant.messages, length(it.text ?? '') > 0), messages: state.assistant.messages}], filter(state.assistant.conversations, it.id != state.assistant.conversation)), 0, 50)}}

assistant.new.note: Starts a new conversation: the one shown is kept with the past ones

assistant.history.note: Shows the past conversations in place of the one shown, or the conversation again

assistant.resume.note: with: id, a past conversation's: it is shown again, to go on with, and the one shown is kept with the past ones

assistant.forget.note: with: id: deletes a past conversation

assistant.allowRun.note: with: id, a run of a command that waits for a yes (the runs variable): it runs now, under its runner's name

assistant.alwaysAllowRun.note: with: id: it runs now, and that peer may run that command again without asking (runGrants)

assistant.undoRun.note: with: id, a run that ran: what it changed in the state is put back

with.title: {{message.title}}
with.status: {{preview != null && preview.id == message.id ? 'previewing' : contains(assistantPending, message.id) ? 'pending' : state.assistant.decided[message.id] ?? 'closed'}}

with.title: {{join(split(run.title || run.command, '\n'), ' ')}}
with.summary: {{run.state == 'waiting' ? (run.personOnly ? t('assistant.run.windowAsks') : t('assistant.run.wants', {author: run.author})) : run.state == 'ran' || run.state == 'undone' ? t('assistant.run.ranFor', {author: run.author}) : run.reason != '' ? t('assistant.run.notRun', {reason: join(split(run.reason, '\n'), ' ')}) : t('assistant.run.notRunBare')}}
with.lines: {{map(map(slice(entries(run.arguments ?? {}), 0, 3), {key: join(split(it.key, '\n'), ' '), letters: split(join(split(type(it.value) == 'string' ? it.value : json(it.value), '\n'), ' '), '')}), it.key + ': ' + join(slice(it.letters, 0, 60), '') + (length(it.letters) > 60 ? '…' : ''))}}

with.items: {{map(assistantModels.models, {title: it.name, checked: it.id == assistantModel, keyLabel: it.id == assistantModels.default ? t('assistant.defaultModel') : '', run: 'assistant.pickModel', with: {id: it.id}})}}
